item.title: Version 1.0
item.description:
Seal 1.0

The free core is free forever, and always was: recording, live transcription at full accuracy, on-device notes, your whole meeting history, search, and Markdown and PDF export. Seal Pro adds the slower, deeper passes — speaker split, asking a meeting questions, follow-up drafts, the maximum-accuracy re-transcribe. One payment, two Macs, and the licence is checked exactly once.

If you were here before this release: thank you. SEALBETA is Seal Pro, free, and the app will show you the code once.

Your models are moving, and it is about time

Until now Seal let its speech models land in your Documents folder, which is where iCloud Drive syncs — some nine gigabytes of model weights quietly uploading themselves, from the app whose whole argument is that nothing leaves your Mac. They now live in Application Support beside the notes model. This update moves the ones you already have rather than downloading them again.

Offline works now, which it did not

A fully downloaded model still asked huggingface.co for a file listing before it would load, so with Wi-Fi off a recording failed at the first word — while the privacy page invited you to try exactly that. A cached model now loads without touching the network at all.

Every voice gets its own colour

Speaker split named the voices and then drew them all in the same green, which told you nothing. Each identified speaker now has a colour of its own — from a palette the app's greens should have joined at the rebrand and didn't.

item.title: Version 0.24
item.description:
The seal turns up

Seal has a face now, and it shows up where it has something to say. The empty screen is a sleeping seal. Start a meeting and, in the stretch after Start and before anyone speaks, it's sitting in the transcript panel with its ears up. A meeting you took no notes in shows it holding a fistful of them. Nothing moves once it has settled in.

The app icon is the seal too, above 32 px — at Finder-list and Spotlight sizes it hands back to the mark, which still reads there.

Two things that were quietly wrong

The sidebar looked tucked under a bar: macOS gives a split view one toolbar strip across both panes, so the flat colour 0.23 painted it was the detail pane's colour sitting over the sidebar. Each pane's own surface now runs to the top of the window. And Settings' header was a different colour from its panes — AppKit's own material, showing through above the tabs.

item.title: Version 0.23
item.description:
A fix for one stubborn spot of the old colour

0.22 changed Seal's accent to forest and lime, but the selected row in the sidebar stayed indigo — the one surface macOS draws for itself, from a place the rest of the theme doesn't reach. It's green now, in both Light and Dark.

That's the whole release. Nothing else changed.

item.title: Version 0.22
item.description:
Seal changes colour, and your licence stops being fragile

  • The accent is forest and lime now — the same palette as sealformac.com, replacing the old indigo. It inverts with your appearance rather than just lightening: deep forest in Light, lime in Dark. That keeps the You and Others speaker labels apart by brightness alone, so they stay readable with red-green colour blindness.
  • Your licence can no longer be overwritten by a bad read. If Seal opened your licence file and couldn't verify it — a moved Keychain, a restored backup, a new Mac — it used to fall back to free and save that over the file, which made a recoverable moment permanent. Now it reads, shrugs, and leaves the file exactly where it is. Nothing is written to your licence unless you activate, deactivate, or start a trial.

No changes to recording, transcription, or notes in this one. As always: no subscription required, no account, nothing leaves your Mac.

item.title: Version 0.21
item.description:
Thank you, beta users

If you were using Seal before Seal Pro existed, this update owes you two things: an explanation and a gift.

  • The explanation, in-app. Recent updates drew the line between free Seal and Seal Pro — quietly, which wasn't fair. This version greets long-time installs once with exactly what changed. The short version: everything you rely on stays free forever, and your meetings are never locked.
  • The gift. Seal Pro is on us: the in-app note carries the code SEALBETA — 100% off at checkout, valid through November 10, 2026. You tested Seal when it was rough; that counts.
  • The upgrade sheet now states the 30-day money-back guarantee, and licensing got a hardening pass: every state is now tested against every gated surface, with the standing guarantees pinned in code — your history and export can never end up behind the paywall.

No new meeting features this time — those were 0.19 and 0.20. As always: no subscription required, no account, nothing leaves your Mac.

item.title: Version 0.20
item.description:
A clearer look at Seal Pro

  • The upgrade sheet is a pitch now, not a spec sheet. A headline that says what Pro is for — and when you open it from a locked button, that feature's own promise leads. Features sit in a scannable icon grid, and the things that make Seal different stand right above the price: pay once and it's yours, everything stays on your Mac, the free core stays free.
  • Activating a license now lands the moment. Instead of the window silently closing, you get a proper welcome: your plan stated plainly, and one button back to work.

Everything else is as it was in 0.19 — and as always: no subscription required, no account, nothing leaves your Mac.

item.title: Version 0.19
item.description:
Pick your microphone — and notes that grew up

  • Choose the microphone. Settings → Recording now has a microphone picker, and the sliders popover in the recording bar carries the same one — switching applies instantly, even mid-meeting. Automatic stays the default and still avoids Bluetooth mics so your headphones keep full-quality sound; an explicit choice always wins. Call-audio capture can also be turned off, to record only yourself.
  • Star the moment. The ★ button in the recording bar and the floating pill — or ⇧⌘H from anywhere — marks what's being said right now as important. The generated notes make a point of covering every starred moment, quoting what was said around it.
  • Bullets, checkboxes, folders. Start a note with "- " for a bullet or "[]" for a checkbox — checked boxes cross out and flow into the meeting's Action items. Right-click a meeting to file it into a folder; the tag field now offers tags you've used before.
  • Quieter, clearer. The recording bar dropped its badge — on-device is the default and needs no announcing (a small amber note appears only if you opt into cloud notes). Every button has a tooltip, mic notices fade after a few seconds instead of staying forever, action items you finished earlier tuck away behind "Show completed", and the notes & transcript view gained a Copy button.

item.title: Version 0.18
item.description:
Who said what — and Seal Pro

  • Seal now tells the far side's voices apart. When a recording stops, the saved call audio goes through speaker identification — on your Mac's Neural Engine, nothing leaves your computer — and the transcript shows Speaker 1, Speaker 2, … as separate turns instead of one "Others". Right-click a line to name a voice; the name follows it through the transcript, exports, and notes. Older meetings get the same with Identify speakers, when their audio was kept. A line Seal can't place with confidence stays unlabeled rather than guessed.
  • Seal Pro. Everything you've been using stays free — unlimited meetings, full-accuracy live transcription, notes, search, and export, forever. Pro gathers the assistant extras: speaker identification, transcript polish, ask-your-meeting, reshaped summaries, follow-up drafts, action tracking, and custom templates. Try it free for 14 days — the trial starts only when you choose, from Settings → License. No account, no subscription, and Seal still never phones home.
  • Seal now lives at sealformac.com.

item.title: Version 0.17
item.description:
Seal notices when your meeting starts — and when it ends

  • When a call app starts using your microphone — Zoom, Teams, Webex, FaceTime, Slack, Discord, or a Meet tab in Chrome, Safari, Arc, Dia, Edge, Brave, or Firefox — a small card floats in: "Record it with Seal?" One click and the meeting is being recorded. Watching for this needs no new permissions, and the signal never leaves your Mac.
  • By default Seal still never records without your click. If you want it to start on its own, there's a new toggle in Settings — off until you turn it on.
  • When every call app has let go of the microphone, Seal stops the recording on its own, saves the meeting, and offers your notes. A drop-and-rejoin doesn't end the meeting, and recordings made outside any call are never touched.

item.title: Version 0.16
item.description:
Company names that survive being misheard

  • Whisper does not only misspell a company it has never heard of — it cuts it into different words. "Aramco" arrives as "a Ramco", "CloudSufi" as "Cloud Sophie", and a correction that reads one word at a time can reach neither. Names in your vocabulary are now matched across several words at once, so they come back whole however they were cut — and the same works in reverse, when two words you wrote down are heard as one.
  • A soft g is heard as a j, which is how one platform came out as "Heijen", "Hagen" and "Heijin" across a single call and never once as "HeyGen". That corrects now too.
  • As before, this only fixes names you have added in Settings → Vocabulary. It stays quiet when it isn't sure, and it will not rename an ordinary word — "QR Code" stays "QR Code" even alongside a name that sounds like it.

item.title: Version 0.15
item.description:
Your other language, transcribed as itself

  • Switch languages mid-meeting and Seal no longer answers in the wrong one. Whisper treats a language setting as a suggestion rather than an instruction, so on Ukrainian speech the English pass would quietly drift into Russian — and then win the transcript anyway, because it still carried English's label. A reading now has to be written in the language that produced it before it counts as that language's reading. On a 64-minute lesson this corrected every Cyrillic line, and left the English untouched.
  • A stray Japanese or Korean word can no longer stand in for a backchannel like "mm-hmm".

item.title: Version 0.14
item.description:
Names spelled right, and a way to tell us when something breaks

  • Add the people you meet with to your vocabulary in Settings and Seal now fixes their spelling in the transcript. When it hears "Demitra" for "Dmytro" or "Krithi" for "Kriti", it corrects it — the consonants are what survive a mishearing, so that is what it matches on. It stays quiet when it isn't sure.
  • Every meeting now has Report a problem in its export menu. It writes up what actually happened during transcription — how much speech was decoded, how much came back empty, what was filtered and why — and shows you the whole thing before anything is sent. It contains no transcript text. The detailed log, which does quote what was said, is attached only if you tick the box.

item.title: Version 0.13
item.description:
Faster, and quieter when nobody is talking

  • If you had added any words to your custom vocabulary, Seal was quietly transcribing almost every passage twice — and occasionally losing one altogether. It now notices when the vocabulary isn't reaching the speech model and stops paying for it.
  • Seal no longer writes "Thank you." into the transcript when a microphone picks up nothing but a pause.

item.title: Version 0.12
item.description:
Speech that was heard no longer goes missing

  • Whole stretches of the other side of a call could vanish from the transcript — a sentence would stop mid-word and pick up half a minute later. The speech recogniser was abandoning a passage whenever it was unsure of the very first word in it, and throwing the rest away with it. On one nine-minute standup that was 45 seconds of talk, an eighth of everything said.
  • A meeting that opens in a language Seal doesn't transcribe — a minute of small talk before the call gets going — no longer starts the transcript off in the wrong alphabet, and can no longer convince Seal that the rest of the meeting is in that language too.

item.title: Version 0.11
item.description:
Tidier meeting titles

  • A title that ran past the space available was cut wherever the limit happened to fall, mid-word — one meeting was filed as "…and Legal Services Compari". Long titles now end on a whole word.

item.title: Version 0.10
item.description:
Meetings no longer lose whole stretches of the conversation

  • The far side of your calls is back. Seal could quietly drop long runs of the other person's speech — in one 64-minute call, 39 minutes of it. Each decode was being cut short before it ever reached your audio, and because it came back empty rather than wrong, nothing anywhere said so. This also turns out to be what pushed some meetings into the wrong language, so 0.9's language fix now holds in cases it could not reach before.
  • And so is your own side. Three separate microphone faults could each lose your half of a meeting: recording from the Mac's built-in mic while you wore AirPods it could not hear you through, the microphone stopping partway through with nothing noticing, and the opening seconds lost while capture restarted itself. Seal now checks that the microphone it picked can actually hear you, keeps watching it for the whole meeting, and restarts it if it drops out.
  • Short answers stop vanishing. "Yes, it is." and other brief replies were being discarded before they were ever transcribed.
  • Notes are written in the language you spoke. An all-English meeting came back summarised and titled in Swedish.

item.title: Version 0.9
item.description:
Transcripts no longer get stuck in the wrong language

  • The big fix. If Seal misheard your first few words as another language, it used to stay stuck there for the rest of the meeting — and quietly discard the lines it had got right. In one 64-minute English lesson, most of one speaker's side came out as Cyrillic. Now the two sides of a call check each other: when the person you are talking to is clearly speaking one language, Seal reconsiders instead of digging in.
  • Genuinely bilingual calls are unaffected. A speaker who has really established their own language keeps it — only a weakly supported guess can be overruled.
  • Each recording now keeps a small diagnostic log beside it, so a transcript that still comes out wrong can be explained instead of guessed at. Like everything else in Seal, it never leaves your Mac.

item.title: Version 0.8
item.description:
Recording no longer disturbs your Mac's audio playback

  • The deeper fix for Bluetooth headphones. 0.7 stopped Seal from using the headset's microphone, but the system-audio capturer itself could still make playback lag, go silent, or disconnect the headset. Seal now captures the Mac's audio through a lighter mechanism that leaves the output device completely untouched.
  • One new permission, one old one retired. The first recording will ask to allow "System Audio Recording" — click Allow. The broader Screen Recording permission is no longer needed.
  • Sessions that start on music no longer open with stray "Music"/"Музика" lines.

item.title: Version 0.7
item.description:
Your headphones keep full audio quality while recording

  • Recording with AirPods (or any Bluetooth headset) no longer ruins playback. Starting a recording used to switch the headset into its low-quality call mode — sound became muffled, choppy, or cut out until the recording stopped. Seal now records from a wired microphone instead (the Mac's built-in mic, or a display microphone), so the headset stays in full-quality music mode. A caption shows which mic is in use.
  • On a Mac with no wired microphone, Seal keeps the headset mic and says playback quality may drop — no more mystery.

item.title: Version 0.6
item.description:
Meeting pages no longer share state with each other

  • "Generating notes" showed on every meeting, not just the one generating. Each AI job (Generate notes, Reshape, Improve transcript, Draft follow-up, Extract actions) now belongs to the meeting it was started for and shows progress only there.
  • Results always land on the right meeting — a finished generation can no longer drop its text into whichever meeting was open, and a title or tag edited while the model worked is no longer reverted when it finishes.
  • Heavy AI jobs no longer stack — one at a time.

item.title: Version 0.5
item.description:
Transcription no longer silently stops mid-meeting

  • A rare glitch could freeze one side of the transcript — audio kept being captured, but no new lines appeared for that speaker until the end of the meeting. The engine's internal jobs now run strictly one at a time, and each has a time limit: if anything ever gets stuck again, Seal abandons that one sentence and keeps going. Worst case changed from "rest of the meeting lost" to "one sentence lost."
  • Two more guards against invented lines in the opening seconds of a recording, before the meeting's language has settled.

If an earlier meeting was affected, its audio is saved — open it and use "Improve transcript" to recover the full text.

item.title: Version 0.4
item.description:
Removes the last way a foreign word could sneak in

  • No more invented words in the wrong alphabet — anywhere in a meeting. After a recording went quiet (a video ended, everyone stopped talking), background noise could still appear as a word like "Дякую." even in an all-English session. A short line written in an alphabet that doesn't match its own language is now recognized as noise and dropped, at any point in a meeting. Real short answers and genuine language switches are untouched.

item.title: Version 0.3
item.description:
Fixes meetings coming out nearly empty on English calls

  • Whole meetings are no longer lost to a language mix-up. Seal read its language detector's answer backwards, so an English call could be treated as "certainly Ukrainian" — the transcript then filtered itself down to a handful of lines, or filled with Cyrillic look-alikes of English words. Detection is now read correctly, and a line needs real evidence before it can pull the meeting toward another language.
  • No more invented words at the start of a recording. The meeting-join chime could appear as "Дякую!" or "you" before anyone spoke. Stock filler words are ignored until someone has actually said something — real greetings still come through.
  • "Improve transcript" fixed too — it had the same backwards reading and could redo an entire English meeting in the wrong language.
  • On Macs with less memory, lines from the very end of a meeting can no longer be silently lost while notes are being prepared.

item.title: Version 0.2
item.description:
Noticeably more accurate transcripts

  • No more Cyrillic in English recordings. Seal could invent Russian or Ukrainian words in places where nobody had actually spoken — in one English-only call, 17% of lines came back in the wrong alphabet. Silence is now read as silence.
  • Repetitive speech is kept. Saying similar phrases in a row, like reading out a list, no longer looks like a stuck decoder, so those words are no longer discarded.
  • Lines appear in the order they were spoken. A reply could previously show up above the remark it answered. Consecutive lines from the same speaker now join into one turn instead of being split at every short pause.

Seal also reports its real version number now, so this is the first release that can keep itself up to date automatically.
